name: Define a feature the product-truth way
summary: The way a person adds a feature to Leafcutter without writing specs by hand: they say in plain language what they want, the system drafts a flow (plus mock data and mockups) they can look at, and once they review and approve it the acceptance criteria are generated from the flow's steps. The flow becomes the reviewable source of truth that the rest of the pipeline builds from.

steps.label: Say what you want
steps.human: The person describes the feature they want in plain language — no spec format, no Gherkin, just intent.

steps.label: System drafts flow · mock · mockups
steps.human: The system turns that intent into a draft flow, a mock-data set, and mockups the person can actually look at and react to.

steps.label: You review & approve; ACs are generated
steps.human: The person reviews the drafted flow and approves it; acceptance criteria are then generated from the flow's steps so the flow stays the source of truth.

acceptance_scenarios.given: a person with a feature idea
acceptance_scenarios.when: they describe it in plain language
acceptance_scenarios.then: the request is captured as intent without requiring any spec or Gherkin format
a draft flow plus its mock data and mockups are produced for the person to review
acceptance criteria are generated from the flow's steps and linked back via step.implements

provenance.note: Real flow describing Leafcutter's own flow-first feature-definition loop.
